binders: field is an arbitrary curried function Real → Real → Real (equivalently, a real-valued function of two real variables).
speed, x, and t are arbitrary real numbers.
conclusions: LocalDef001(field,speed,x,t) holds if and only if LocalDef002(field,speed,x,t) holds.

After expanding both abbreviations, the conclusion is P(field,speed,x,t) ↔ P(field,speed,x,t), where P says that there exist real numbers qt and qx such that tau ↦ field(x,tau) has derivative qt at t, xi ↦ field(xi,t) has derivative qx at x, and qt + speed * qx = 0.
mathematical_definitions: Define P(q,c,x,t) to mean: there exist qt,qx ∈ Real for which the second-variable slice tau ↦ q(x,tau) is differentiable at t with derivative qt, the first-variable slice xi ↦ q(xi,t) is differentiable at x with derivative qx, and qt + c qx = 0.
LocalDef001(q,c,x,t) and LocalDef002(q,c,x,t) are both definitionally equal to P(q,c,x,t).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real-valued function field of two real variables and all real numbers speed, x, and t, if speed is positive, then the following two statements are logically equivalent: there exist the two pointwise partial-derivative values of field at (x,t) and they satisfy qt + speed*qx = 0; and that very same statement. Thus the conclusion is a self-equivalence of one pointwise differential condition.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The implication is restricted to strictly positive speed; it asserts nothing for speed = 0 or speed < 0.
The function field is otherwise completely arbitrary. No global differentiability, continuity, regularity, domain condition, initial condition, or boundary condition is assumed or concluded.
The differential condition is only pointwise at the selected pair (x,t), using derivatives of the two one-variable slices there.

The theorem does not assert that either side's differential condition is true. Since both sides expand to exactly the same proposition, the equivalence holds whether that common proposition is true or false.
If either required partial derivative fails to exist, the common existential proposition is false on both sides, so the equivalence still holds.
The positive-speed hypothesis is not used to distinguish the two sides and is unnecessary for the expanded self-equivalence.
No characteristic formula, transport identity between values at different points, uniqueness statement, or evolution claim is encoded.
